pecorino-tenero-3-mesi: Soft pecorino aged 3 months, with a delicate and aromatic flavour. Soft and elastic paste, perfect for cheese boards, sandwiches, starters and everyday cooking.
More information
📍 Origin
Produced in Sardinia, in the pastoral areas of Barbagia, Marmilla, Ogliastra and Logudoro, where making pecorino is an art handed down through generations.
The milk comes from Sardinian sheep raised on free pasture, rich in wild herbs and Mediterranean scrub.
🧀 What it is
Pecorino tenero 3 mesi is a short-aged sheep's cheese, made from whole sheep's milk.
After about 90 days of maturing, it has:
a soft, elastic and still moist paste,
a thin, natural rind,
a sweet, slightly milky and pleasant flavour.
It is a versatile cheese, perfect for the whole family.
👃 Flavours and aromatic profile
Sweet and delicate taste
Fresh, milky aroma, with light herbaceous notes
Light saltiness, well balanced
Soft paste, pleasant to cut
Harmonious, unobtrusive aftertaste
🍽️ Recommended pairings
With other foods
Pane Carasau, Civraxiu or soft bread rolls
Young Sardinian cured meats: prosciutto crudo, pancetta, sweet sausage
Citrus or wildflower honey, or pear/fig jam
Grilled vegetables, courgettes, aubergines, peppers
Fresh tomatoes, olives, summer salads
Excellent melted on pizzas, focaccias or bruschetta
With drinks
Fresh white wines: Vermentino, Nuragus, Semidano
Mineral and fruity rosé wines
Light red wines: Monica, young Cannonau
Pale or unfiltered craft beers
Also perfect with dry sparkling wines
✨ Use in the kitchen
Ideal for fresh, light cheese boards
Perfect for sandwiches, starters and aperitifs
Excellent melted in cooking (pizzas, pasta, vegetables)
Excellent in salads or summer dishes
Perfect for creamy, delicately flavoured recipes
pecorino-semistagionato-8-mesi: Sardinian semi-aged pecorino, 8 months, with a balanced, aromatic and slightly sharp flavour. Compact paste, rich in Mediterranean aromas. A versatile cheese, ideal for cheese boards, cooking and tastings.
Produced in Sardinia, particularly in the pastoral areas of Barbagia, Ogliastra, Marmilla and Logudoro, where the pecorino tradition has been handed down through generations.
The milk comes from Sardinian sheep raised at pasture, fed on wild herbs and Mediterranean scrub.
Pecorino semistagionato 8 mesi is a hard cheese made from whole sheep's milk.
After production, the wheels are left to mature for about 240 days, developing:
a compact paste that is still soft in the mouth,
a full but not excessive aromatic profile.
It is the perfect meeting point between the sweetness of young pecorino and the intensity of aged pecorino.
Savoury, balanced taste, with a light natural sharpness
Notes of hay, Mediterranean herbs and mature milk
Sardinian cured meats: prosciutto crudo, aged sausage, pancetta, mustela
Grilled vegetables, mushrooms, artichokes and potatoes
Sardinian red wines: Cannonau, Bovale, Carignano, Monica
Full-bodied white wines: Vermentino superiore, dry Nasco
Craft beers: amber, strong ale, unfiltered
Also excellent with white mirto or filu 'e ferru at the end of a meal
Excellent melted on pizzas, focaccias, vegetables
Perfect for grating over first courses
Perfect enjoyed in shavings with honey or jams
pecorino-stagionato-10-mesi: Sardinian aged pecorino, 10 months, with a bold but balanced flavour. Intense aroma, hard paste and rich taste. Ideal for cheese boards, cooking and traditional tastings.
Produced in the pastoral areas of Sardinia: particularly Barbagia, Ogliastra, Marmilla and Logudoro, territories with a long tradition of working sheep's milk.
Sardinian sheep graze freely and feed on wild herbs, giving the milk a unique aromatic profile.
Pecorino stagionato 10 mesi is a hard sheep's cheese, made from whole sheep's milk and given a long but harmonious maturing.
During its 10 months of aging it develops:
It is a cheese with character, yet still mellow in its complexity.
Herbaceous notes, hay and dried fruit/nuts
Long, harmonious aftertaste, typical of mature Sardinian pecorino
Sardinian cured meats: aged sausage, mustela, lonza, prosciutto crudo
Chestnut or strawberry-tree honey (ideal for contrast)
Pear, fig or red onion jams
Excellent in shavings or grated over:
Full-bodied Sardinian red wines: Cannonau, Carignano del Sulcis, Bovale, Mandrolisai
Important white wines: Vermentino superiore, dry Nasco
Craft beers: amber or strong ale
Also excellent with spirits such as filu 'e ferru or white mirto
Ideal for grating over first courses and soups
Excellent in rustic and traditional recipes
Perfect enjoyed in shavings with honey or jams
